SOURCE-TRACEABILITY REPAIR - review-fix cycle 2, finding 13. AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE LINKAGE FOR THIS FEATURE.

VERIFIED DURABLE SOURCE STASH: E9E5E6CC. It IS present and tracked at HEAD in `.backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl` (git blob aef5f126cca7bcb18a5284a16789a1dfec252fd4). The cycle-2 reviewer reported it as "not found in active or archived stash"; that report is a FALSE POSITIVE arising from a lookup against the ACTIVE stash only. Consumed entries are moved to the archive by the harvest workflow, so `.backlogit/stash/` is empty by design and `backlogit stash get E9E5E6CC` correctly returns not-found - the entry is archived, not missing. The durable record is the archive JSONL, which is tracked in Git and auditable at any commit.

ARCHIVE IMMUTABILITY (why the stale annotation is NOT rewritten): the archived entry carries a HARVESTED annotation naming "tasks 160.001-T..160.011-T, shipment 168-S", which was accurate at the moment of the cycle-1 harvest and is now numerically stale. backlogit exposes no supported operation to amend an archived stash entry (`stash edit` addresses active entries only), and that is correct behaviour rather than a gap: an archive record states what was true when the harvest occurred, and retroactively editing it would falsify the audit trail it exists to provide. The stale range is therefore preserved deliberately as a point-in-time record, and THIS COMMENT on the live feature artifact is the supported forward-repair - the durable, queryable statement of current scope.

CURRENT AUTHORITATIVE SCOPE (supersedes the archived annotation's task range): 19 tasks, 160.001-T through 160.019-T, all members of shipment 168-S (20 members including this feature). The four tasks added in review-fix cycle 2 are 160.016-T (characterization harness), 160.017-T (transition ledger), 160.018-T (schema publication and contract registration), 160.019-T (sdist wiring).

AB387F16 - NO DURABLE RECORD EXISTS AND NONE WILL BE FABRICATED. This identifier appears only as "supersedes temporary ID AB387F16" in this feature's own record. It was a pre-persistence temporary identifier assigned before the stash entry was durably written; no stash entry, active or archived, was ever created under it. It is intentionally left with no backing record. Manufacturing a stash entry to satisfy a traceability lookup would create false provenance - a fabricated record is strictly worse than an honestly absent one, because it is indistinguishable from a real one on later audit. E9E5E6CC is the sole durable source of this feature and the only ID that should be followed.

AUDIT PATH: feature 160-F -> this comment -> `.backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl` entry E9E5E6CC (tracked at HEAD) -> plan docs/plans/2026-09-03-minimal-copilot-plugin-payload-plan.md (Traceability section) -> shipment 168-S (20 members).

HOUSEKEEPING: the immediately preceding one-word comment 'probe' was a tool-availability verification no-op emitted while confirming that the comment-append path had succeeded (the CLI returns no stdout on success). It carries no decision, no scope, and no traceability content, and should be ignored on audit. It is left in place rather than removed because this log is append-only by design and rewriting it would be a worse defect than the noise. The authoritative record is the SOURCE-TRACEABILITY REPAIR comment immediately before it.

HOUSEKEEPING: the immediately preceding comment event on this log is EMPTY. It was written by an append_comment call that supplied the comment text under a wrong parameter name, so the tool recorded a well-formed event with no body. It carries no meaning, supersedes nothing, and is superseded by nothing. It is left in place rather than excised because this log is append-only by design and rewriting it to hide a harmless no-op would be a worse defect than the no-op. The substantive cycle-3 traceability correction is the comment that follows this one.

SOURCE-TRACEABILITY FORWARD CORRECTION (review-fix cycle 3, finding 11) - SUPERSEDES THE CYCLE-2 "SOURCE-TRACEABILITY REPAIR" COMMENT ON THIS FEATURE.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The authoritative harvest annotation on archived stash entry E9E5E6CC records the harvest scope as "160.001-T..160.011-T" - true when it was written, and now incomplete: review-fix cycles 1 and 2 split and added tasks, taking the feature to nineteen. E9E5E6CC is an ARCHIVED stash record and is therefore IMMUTABLE by design; hand-editing the archive so an old annotation says something it did not say at the time would destroy the historical fact that the harvest originally produced eleven tasks, and would make the archive an unreliable witness for every other entry in it. The correction is therefore recorded FORWARD, here, on the live feature, through the official comment surface - the annotation stays true about the past, and this comment is authoritative about the present.

WHY THE CYCLE-2 CORRECTION WAS NOT SUFFICIENT. It expressed scope as a RANGE ("160.001-T through 160.019-T"). A range silently asserts that the interval is dense. If any ID in it were absent, retired, or belonged to another feature, the range would still read as correct while being wrong, and no consumer could detect it. This comment therefore ENUMERATES every member explicitly, so the chain is verifiable member-by-member rather than merely trusted.

Every one of the eight descends from E9E5E6CC through this feature; none has an independent source, and none is orphaned.

AB387F16 IS NOT FABRICATED AND MUST NOT BE. It was a pre-persistence temporary working ID, superseded by E9E5E6CC before any stash record was ever written. It has NO durable stash entry, and one must not be created for it: manufacturing a record to satisfy a lookup would invent provenance that never existed and would be a worse outcome than the absence it resolves. Its correct and complete disposition is this note plus the superseded-ID note in the feature body.

AUTHORITY. Where this comment and any earlier traceability statement disagree about the CURRENT task set, this comment governs. Where they disagree about what was true AT HARVEST TIME, the archived E9E5E6CC annotation governs. The two never actually conflict, because they describe different moments.

REFERENCED BY: the 160-F feature body, and docs/plans/2026-09-03-minimal-copilot-plugin-payload-plan.md section "Traceability".

SOURCE-TRACEABILITY BLOB-REFERENCE CORRECTION (extended review-fix cycle 4, finding 13) - NARROWLY SUPERSEDES ONE CLAIM IN THE CYCLE-2 AND CYCLE-3 TRACEABILITY COMMENTS ON THIS FEATURE. Everything else in those two comments STANDS.

WHAT IS WRONG. Both prior comments pin the durable source stash entry with a WHOLE-FILE GIT BLOB HASH described as current "at HEAD":
  cycle 2: "It IS present and tracked at HEAD in `.backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl` (git blob aef5f126cca7bcb18a5284a16789a1dfec252fd4)"
  cycle 3: "E9E5E6CC (archived stash entry; durable and tracked at HEAD in .backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl, blob aef5f126)"
That blob hash identifies the ENTIRE `.backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl` FILE, not the entry E9E5E6CC inside it. The archive is APPEND-ONLY AND STILL BEING WRITTEN - review-fix cycle 3 alone archived duplicate stash entry 9938CA1D under finding 12 - so every archive mutation produces a NEW file blob and INVALIDATES the pin. The claim was true when written and is now STALE.

MEASURED, AT THIS COMMIT.
  Branch: chore/stage-159-167-publication
  HEAD: a03a6ff05b1faedfd13b66984933a76f59d1b338
  `git rev-parse HEAD:.backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl` -> 7a92cc5fcfe0b85cf26a7d941657177e6dde5032
  `git rev-parse 35c081d5:.backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl` -> aef5f126cca7bcb18a5284a16789a1dfec252fd4
So aef5f126 was the file blob at commit 35c081d5 ("chore(stage): plan minimal Copilot plugin payload"), NOT at HEAD. A reader resolving `aef5f126` today and finding it is not the HEAD blob has no way, from the prior comments alone, to tell whether the entry moved, was rewritten, or was lost.

THE CORRECTED REFERENCE - DURABLE IDENTITY FIRST, BLOB REFERENCE ALWAYS COMMIT-QUALIFIED.
1. THE AUTHORITATIVE, STABLE REFERENCE IS THE ENTRY ID PLUS ITS PATH: stash entry **E9E5E6CC** in **`.backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl`**. The entry ID is assigned once and never changes; the path is stable; and together they survive every future append to the archive. This is what downstream artifacts should cite.
2. A BLOB HASH IS A POINT-IN-TIME REFERENCE AND MUST ALWAYS BE WRITTEN COMMIT-QUALIFIED, never as "at HEAD": `35c081d5:.backlogit/archive/stash.jsonl` = blob aef5f126cca7bcb18a5284a16789a1dfec252fd4. In that form the reference stays TRUE FOREVER, because it names the commit it is true of. The bare-hash-plus-"at HEAD" form was guaranteed to rot on the next archive write.
3. The current whole-file blob at HEAD a03a6ff0 is 7a92cc5f. THIS FIGURE IS ITSELF POINT-IN-TIME and will change on the next archive append; it is recorded as measurement evidence, NOT as a new pin to cite. Do not replace one rotting pin with another.

NO HISTORY IS REWRITTEN. The two prior comments are NOT edited or deleted, and archived entry E9E5E6CC is NOT touched - the archive is immutable by design, and the append-only comment log is the supported forward-repair surface. This correction is APPENDED through the official comment operation, exactly as the cycle-2 and cycle-3 corrections were.

SCOPE OF SUPERSESSION - DELIBERATELY NARROW. This comment supersedes ONLY the blob-reference form and the "at HEAD" qualifier. It does NOT disturb: the finding that E9E5E6CC is present, tracked and auditable; the cycle-3 ENUMERATED provenance chain E9E5E6CC -> 160-F -> the nineteen tasks -> 168-S; the reasoning that the archived harvest annotation stays true about the past; or the AB387F16 disposition (no durable record exists, and none will be fabricated). Where this comment and any earlier statement disagree about HOW TO REFERENCE the archived entry, this comment governs; on every other subject the cycle-3 comment remains authoritative.
